instruction: Rename picture1.jpg in your Pictures folder to 'Kilimanjaro.jpg'.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened Files, navigated to Pictures, right-clicked and renamed all 3 picture files. Got picture1→Mount Kilimanjaro (correct), picture2→Mount Everest (correct), but picture3→Mount Kailash (wrong, should be Huashan). Score 0 because evaluator requires all correct.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open file manager, navigate directories, right-click files, use Rename dialog, type new names. Successfully performed 3 rename operations.
metadata.failure_analysis: Model misidentified picture3 (Huashan/Mount Hua plank path) as Mount Kailash. The all-or-nothing evaluator gave 0 despite 2/3 correct renames.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to a single file rename with the name provided in the instruction - no mountain identification needed. Tests basic file renaming capability that model demonstrated.
metadata.explanation: Task asks to rename one specific file. Getter lists files in Pictures directory. Metric checks new name exists (0.7) and old name is gone (0.3).

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly lists files in /home/user/Pictures/ directory using ls, returning a structured dict with file list

Metric correctly handles expected parameter - since expected.type='rule', it receives {'new_name': 'Kilimanjaro.jpg', 'old_name': 'picture1.jpg'} directly and accesses keys properly with expected.get('new_name') and expected.get('old_name')
Complete coverage: the single instruction requirement (rename picture1.jpg to Kilimanjaro.jpg) is fully verified by checking both presence of new filename (0.7) and absence of old filename (0.3)
Scoring breakdown is reasonable: 0.7 for new file existing gives majority credit for the rename, 0.3 for old file removal confirms it was a rename not a copy
Error handling is adequate: getter handles directory listing failure, metric handles string/error results with short-circuit evaluation
